relevance_reason: The paper identifies GPX4 mutations as the cause of Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia in two families.

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2014) described Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia (SSMD) as a neonatal lethal form of spondylometaphyseal dysplasia characterized by severe metaphyseal chondrodysplasia with mild limb shortening, platyspondyly, cardiac conduction defects, and central nervous system abnormalities.
quotes: Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia (SSMD) is a neonatal lethal form of spondylometaphyseal dysplasia characterised by severe metaphyseal chondrodysplasia with mild limb shortening, platyspondyly, cardiac conduction defects, and central nervous system abnormalities.

findings.statement: By whole exome sequencing of a girl with SSMD and her unaffected parents, Smith et al. (2014) identified compound heterozygous variants in GPX4 (NM_001039848.1): a maternally inherited c.587+5G>A splice variant, which in vitro studies showed caused splicing out of part of exon 4, resulting in frameshift and premature truncation.
quotes: Whole exome sequencing of a child affected with SSMD and her unaffected parents identified two rare variants in GPX4. The first (c.587+5G>A) was inherited from the mother, and the second (c.588-8_588-4del) was de novo (NM_001039848.1); both were predicted to impact splicing of GPX4.
In vitro studies confirmed the mutations spliced out part of exon 4 and skipped exon 5, respectively, with both resulting in a frameshift and premature truncation of GPX4.

findings.statement: In the same girl with SSMD, Smith et al. (2014) identified a de novo GPX4 variant, c.588-8_588-4del (NM_001039848.1), in trans with the maternally inherited c.587+5G>A; in vitro studies showed that it caused skipping of exon 5, resulting in frameshift and premature truncation of GPX4.
quotes: The first (c.587+5G>A) was inherited from the mother, and the second (c.588-8_588-4del) was de novo (NM_001039848.1); both were predicted to impact splicing of GPX4.
In vitro studies confirmed the mutations spliced out part of exon 4 and skipped exon 5, respectively, with both resulting in a frameshift and premature truncation of GPX4.

findings.statement: In a second, unrelated child with SSMD whose DNA was not available, Smith et al. (2014) found by Sanger sequencing that both unaffected parents carried the same heterozygous nonsense mutation in exon 3 of GPX4, c.381C>A (p.Tyr127*) (NM_001039848.1).
quotes: Subsequently, a second child with SSMD was identified; although DNA from the child was not available, the two unaffected parents were found by Sanger sequencing to each carry the same heterozygous stop mutation in exon 3 of GPX4, c.381C>A, p.Tyr127* (NM_001039848.1).

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2014) concluded that truncating GPX4 mutations in 2 families with SSMD supported a pathogenic role for GPX4, an antioxidant enzyme that protects cells against membrane lipid peroxidation and is essential for early embryo development. They suggested that their findings highlighted the importance of GPX4 in development of the cardiac, nervous, and skeletal systems.
quotes: Our identification of truncating mutations in GPX4 in two families affected with SSMD supports the pathogenic role of mutated GPX4 in this very rare disease.
Our findings highlight the importance of this enzyme in development of the cardiac, nervous, and skeletal systems.

relevance_reason: This case report describes a patient with Sedaghatian-type SMD who had CNS malformations.

findings.statement: Aygun et al. (2012) reported a patient with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia. The patient had metaphyseal dysplasia, congenital atrioventricular block, a simplified gyral pattern, hypogenesis of the corpus callosum, and severe cerebellar hypoplasia. The authors suggested that central nervous system malformations might be a major component of this congenital lethal skeletal dysplasia and should be evaluated in detail.
quotes: We report on a patient with Sedaghatian type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia (SSMD) who presented with metaphyseal dysplasia, congenital atrioventricular block, simplified gyral pattern, hypogenesis of corpus callosum, and severe cerebellar hypoplasia.
central nervous system malformations might be a major component of the disorder and should be evaluated in detail to possibly uncover the underlying pathophysiology

relevance_reason: Case report of a patient with Sedaghatian SMD that widens the phenotype to include pachygyria and agenesis of the corpus callosum.

findings.statement: English et al. (2006) reported a female infant with Sedaghatian spondylometaphyseal dysplasia. She was born to nonconsanguineous Caucasian parents and had a metaphyseal dysplasia. She was hypotonic from birth and had recurrent cyanotic episodes within a few hours of delivery. Brain imaging showed absence of the corpus callosum and marked frontotemporal pachygyria. She developed seizures on day 14 and died at age 17 days.
quotes: We report on a female infant with a metaphyseal dysplasia and a neuronal migration abnormality consistent with a diagnosis of Sedaghatian spondylometaphyseal dysplasia.
This child, born to nonconsanguineous Caucasian parents, was hypotonic from birth and experienced recurrent cyanotic episodes within a few hours of delivery.
Cerebral imaging revealed absence of the corpus callosum and marked frontotemporal pachygyria. She developed seizures on day 14 of life and died at the age of 17 days.

phenotypes.onset: within a few hours of delivery

findings.statement: English et al. (2006) concluded that their case showed neuronal migration abnormalities can occur in Sedaghatian spondylometaphyseal dysplasia. They suggested agenesis of the corpus callosum as a new association of the disorder.
quotes: Our case highlights the possibility for neuronal migration abnormalities in Sedaghatian spondylometaphyseal dysplasia and suggests a novel association of the disorder with agenesis of the corpus callosum.

relevance_reason: Case report of Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia in a Yemeni infant who lived unusually long.

findings.statement: Koutouby et al. (2000) reported an infant with spondylometaphyseal dysplasia born to nonconsanguineous Yemeni parents. The radiologic findings were consistent with lethal metaphyseal chondrodysplasia, Sedaghatian type. All previously reported patients had died within 4 days of life, but this patient survived 161 days.
quotes: We report a case of spondylometaphyseal dysplasia in an infant who was born to nonconsanguineous Yemeni parents. Radiological findings were consistent with lethal metaphyseal chondrodysplasia (Sedaghatian type).
Although all previously reported cases died within 4 days of life, our patient survived 161 days.

findings.statement: Koutouby et al. (2000) investigated the patient with serum calcium, magnesium, zinc, ammonia, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase and parathormone levels, liver and renal function tests, TORCH, metabolic screening, chromosomal studies, muscle enzymes, EEG, CT scan and brain MRI. Genomic DNA from the patient and parents was analyzed, but no gene abnormality was found.
quotes: This reported case was thoroughly investigated for serum calcium, magnesium, zinc, ammonia, phosphate level, alkaline phosphatase, parathormone level, liver and renal function test, TORCH, metabolic screening, skeletal survey, chromosomal studies, muscle enzymes, EEG, computed tomography scan, and magnetic resonance imaging (brain).
Genomic DNA analysis of patient and parents were sent to the Faculty de Medicine Xavier Bichat, France, but yet abnormal gene could not be detected.

relevance_reason: Reports radiological findings in two unrelated cases of Sedaghatian-type SMD and identifies additional anomalies from a literature review.

findings.statement: Elçioglu and Hall (1998) reported the radiological findings in 2 unrelated cases of spondylometaphyseal dysplasia, Sedaghatian type. After reviewing the literature, they identified additional anomalies, including disproportionately long fibulae, dysharmonious maturation, and turricephaly.
quotes: We present the radiological findings in two unrelated cases with spondylometaphyseal dysplasia type Sedaghatian.
We review the literature and identify additional anomalies including disproportionately long fibulae, dysharmonious maturation and turricephaly.

relevance_reason: This is the original report of the disorder: two affected brothers with congenital lethal metaphyseal chondrodysplasia, and an affected sister mentioned.

findings.statement: Sedaghatian (1980) reported 2 brothers, born within a year of each other, with a similar skeletal disorder. It consisted of severe congenital metaphyseal involvement, mild rhizomelic shortness of the upper limbs, and mild platyspondyly. Both died at 3 days of age of cardiorespiratory insufficiency.
quotes: This is a report of two brothers, born within a year of each other, with a similar skeletal disorder of severe congenital metaphyseal involvement, mild rhizomelic shortness of upper limbs, and mild platyspondyly.
Both died at three days of cardio-respiratory insufficiency

phenotypes.text: mild rhizomelic shortness of upper limbs

findings.statement: Sedaghatian (1980) found that only one of the 2 affected brothers had laboratory tests before death. These showed low calcium, high phosphorus, and high alkaline phosphatase levels, which were attributed to a renal defect.
quotes: only one had ante-mortem lab tests which showed low calcium, high phosphorus, and high alkaline phosphatase levels attributed to a renal defect

findings.statement: Sedaghatian (1980) reported that autopsy of the same infant showed pulmonary, renal, and adrenal hemorrhage, along with subendocardial myocarditis and myocardial necrosis. The author stated that the pathogenetic relationship between these manifestations was unclear.
quotes: On autopsy this same infant was found to have pulmonary, renal and adrenal hemorrhage, and subendocardial myocarditis and myocardial necrosis.
The pathogenetic relationship between these manifestations is presently unclear

findings.statement: The parents of the affected brothers reported by Sedaghatian (1980) were normal and had recently had an affected baby girl. On this basis the author presumed autosomal recessive inheritance.
quotes: since parents are normal and recently had an affected baby girl, it is presumed that this disorder is an autosomal recessive trait

relevance_reason: The paper reports a second Iranian family with Sedaghatian congenital lethal metaphyseal chondrodysplasia, including histopathology, and discusses inheritance.

findings.statement: Opitz et al. (1987) reported another Iranian infant with Sedaghatian syndrome who died on day 4 of life. Histology showed severe epimetaphyseal dysplasia.
quotes: Here data are presented on another Iranian infant with the Sedaghatian syndrome who died on day 4 and was found to have histologic evidence of severe epimetaphyseal dysplasia.

findings.statement: Opitz et al. (1987) summarized Sedaghatian's 1980 report of 2 brothers and a sister with a neonatally lethal disorder marked by slight rhizomelic limb shortening, mild platyspondyly, and severe metaphyseal dysplasia. They suggested the syndrome may be more complexly pleiotropic than the radiographs indicate, because one of Sedaghatian's patients also had microphthalmia, asymmetric ears, depressed nasal bridge, broad nose, short neck, prominent sternum, and short lower extremities.
quotes: In 1980, Sedaghatian described in two brothers and one sister a neonatally lethal disorder associated with slight rhizomelic limb shortness, mild platyspondyly, and severe metaphyseal dysplasia.
since one of Sedaghatian's patients also had "microphthalmia, asymmetry of ears, depressed nasal bridge, broad nose, short neck, prominent sternum, and short lower extremities."

findings.statement: Opitz et al. (1987) suggested that Sedaghatian syndrome is an autosomal recessive trait with a high gene frequency in Iranians. Their reasons were that children of both sexes were affected in one family, the parents were normal first cousins, and the disorder had so far been seen only in Iranians.
quotes: The occurrence in children of both sexes in one instance, born to normal parents who were first cousins, and currently apparent confinement of the disorder to Iranians suggests that the Sedaghatian syndrome is an autosomal recessive trait with high gene frequency in Iranians.

relevance_reason: The paper reports another infant with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia who had a lethal course, and it reviews the earlier Iranian cases. Only the abstract was available.

findings.statement: Peeden et al. (1992) reported another infant with spondylometaphyseal dysplasia, Sedaghatian type, who had a lethal course.
quotes: We report our findings of another infant with a lethal course.

findings.statement: Peeden et al. (1992) reviewed the Iranian infant described by Sedaghatian in 1980, who died shortly after birth. At autopsy he had subacute myocarditis, cortical necrosis of the kidneys, and adrenal and pulmonary hemorrhage. His skeletal findings were mild rhizomelic shortening of the limbs, platyspondyly, and 'laciness' of the iliac wings.
quotes: In 1980 Sedaghatian described an Iranian infant who died shortly after birth. At autopsy, he was found to have subacute myocarditis, cortical necrosis of kidneys, and adrenal and pulmonary hemorrhage.
His skeletal abnormalities included mild rhizomelic shortness of his limbs and platyspondylyl and "laciness" of the iliac wings.

findings.statement: Peeden et al. (1992) noted that the second reported Iranian infant, described by Opitz et al. in 1987, had a similar perinatal course and similar radiographs. Because this infant was born to first-cousin parents, the authors suggested autosomal recessive inheritance of a single-gene defect.
quotes: In 1987 Optiz et al. described another Iranian infant with a similar perinatal course and roentgenograms. This infant was born to first cousins, suggesting an autosomal recessive single gene defect.
